notes: Every number in this file is printed verbatim in a cited source page. Nothing here is
converted, averaged or inferred - derivations (annual retention -> monthly churn) live in
calibration/__init__.py so the arithmetic is inspectable and testable rather than baked in.
Retention figures are stored as ANNUAL retention percentages exactly as the source prints
them. The monthly/annual confusion is the single most likely failure in this pipeline, so
the raw unit is preserved and conversion is explicit and one place only.
ARPA band boundaries follow ChartMogul's own segmentation, which splits $250-500 and
$500-1k. The original target schema merged those into one $250-1000 band; merging two
published medians would have produced a number no source prints, so the source's bands win.
SCHEMA v2 CORRECTION: v1 carried an overall department-median spend table (sales 15%,
marketing 8%, R&D 22%, ...) taken from the SaaS Capital web page via a single
model-mediated read. Those figures could NOT be verified against the report PDF - pages
5-10 are chart images with no extractable text - so they have been removed. Only the
$3-5M ARR band breakdown and the total-spend figures survive verification.

arpa_bands.caveat: 2023 edition. The 2024 retention report (The New Normal, 2,500+ businesses) shows NRR declining across segments since, so these retention figures are likely optimistic for 2026. Its own ARPA chart is an image with no extractable text, so it could not be used to update these.

price_elasticity.reason: No public SaaS price-elasticity dataset exists. The -0.9..-0.2 range currently in apply_pricing_effect is folk knowledge, not measurement. Only first-party A/B price tests identify it; until the decisions table carries price-change events with before/after conversion, this lever must be reported as unidentified rather than as a point estimate.

marketing_saturation_absolute.reason: No public SaaS marketing-saturation dataset exists; open MMM datasets are synthetic and retail-shaped. Not a data gap - a dimensional error. gamma was a bare spend level with no reference to who was being bought. Reparameterised as customers_at_half_saturation * CAC so it scales with the company.
marketing_saturation_absolute.unblocked_by: already fixed structurally; SATURATION_ACQUISITION_RATE remains assumed
